# Zephyrium Docs

> Documentation for Zephyrium, a privacy-preserving layer-1 chain with the ZEP coin.

This file contains links to documentation sections following the llmstxt.org standard.

## Table of Contents

- [Concepts](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/get-started/concepts): What Zephyrium keeps private, how the chain is structured, and its current limits.
- [Quick start](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/get-started/quick-start): Build, launch and check a local Zephyrium devnet.
- [ZEP Documentation](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/): Run a node, validate, and build on the Zephyrium privacy chain.
- [iDEX](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/idex): The exchange built into the Zephyrium chain.
- [iTokens](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/itokens): Private tokens on Zephyrium.
- [iWallet](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/iwallet): The browser-extension wallet for Zephyrium.
- [Differences from Incognito](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/differences-from-incognito): What Zephyrium changed, what it kept, and the naming table.
- [Architecture](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/architecture): Incognito is a privacy-protecting blockchain. It uses peer-to-peer technology to operate with no central authority. Activities and transactions are...
- [Burn address](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/burning-address): * Burn address: is a special address on Incognito chain, which is not accessible by anyone, since no one owns the private keys to that address.
- [Curve](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/edrwards25519): At the first stage of the Incognito project, we use the P-256 ECC library built-in of Golang to implement cryptography protocols. However, the perf...
- [Ethereum bridge](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/ethereum-bridge): Enabling private ETH/ERC20 transactions via a fully decentralized bridge between Incognito and Ethereum
- [Block finality](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/finality-pbft): VOTE PHASE Each validator validate and broadcast its vote for the block
- [Transaction fees](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/min-transaction-fees): **Designers:** @0xankylosaurus, @0xmerman @duyhtq
- [DEX, first design](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/pdex): **Designers:** @0xankylosaurus, @0xgazeka, @hieu013, @duyhtq
- [Committee rotation](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/protocol/upstream/validator-random-substitution): Designers: @0xmerman, @duyhtq, @thaibao-incognito
- [Changelog](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/changelog): What Zephyrium has changed, by date.
- [Origins and credits](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/credits): Zephyrium is a fork of Incognito Chain.
- [Roadmap](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/roadmap): Planned work, in order.
- [ZEP tokenomics](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/tokenomics/zep): The ZEP supply cap, minting schedule and how every block reward is split.
- [Network parameters](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/network-parameters): Every devnet setting and where it lives.
- [Node types](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/node-types): The four kinds of node, what each does and what it needs.
- [Validators and rewards](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/overview): Stake amounts, how a validator gets a seat, and how rewards are split.
